title: Retainage Kept Back for Work the Owner Has Not Paid For
content:
# Retainage Kept Back for Work the Owner Has Not Paid For

Retainage on a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects follows the money: what the owner has not paid for keeps its retainage where it is.

## Rule

Where an amount stands unpaid on the project's contract billings and retainage stands held on it, the releasable retainage is the retainage held less the class's retainage rate taken on the amount standing unpaid, the retainage on work the owner has not paid for staying where it is.

Where nothing stands unpaid on the contract billings and retainage stands held, the whole of the retainage held is releasable.

Where no retainage stands held on the project, nothing is releasable.

## The amount standing unpaid

The amount standing unpaid on the contract billings is the deposit, mobilisation, progress and change order billings raised on the project less the retainage withheld from them and less every payment received, and late fees and remobilisation fees are no part of it. Where payments and retainage together come to more than those billings, nothing stands unpaid.

## Cases (hypothetical, class retainage rate of 10 per cent)

| Retainage held | Amount standing unpaid | Releasable retainage |
|---|---|---|
| USD 20000 | USD 50000 | USD 15000, the held retainage less 10 per cent of 50000 |
| USD 20000 | nothing | USD 20000 |
| nothing | USD 50000 | nothing |

A project whose contract billings come to USD 500000, with USD 50000 of retainage withheld from them and USD 400000 received in payments, has USD 50000 standing unpaid. A late fee of USD 900 also sitting on that project does not enter the figure.
